messages:
maya: quick Q — saw a handful of Secrets in staging not update after a terraform apply that changed Vault KV values. anyone seen a ~1-2m delay with ExternalSecrets polling?

tom: yep, saw similar last week. usually down to poll/resync config or a conflicting k8s resource. which operator + chart are you on?

maya: external-secrets operator (the external-secrets.io one) v0.6 installed via helm. chart values mostly default. terraform does the vault kv write, then we expect ES to pull and reconcile almost immediately but `kubectl get secret` still has old value for ~90s.

nina: 2 quick checks: 1) is there a Terraform-managed `kubernetes_secret` for the same name? if TF owns the Secret it will stomp. 2) what's the ExternalSecret resource spec — are you setting `spec.refreshInterval` or relying on the chart default?

maya: good call, i'm pretty sure we have a tf resource in the repo for the secret (from old flow). i'll check. externalsecret was created by helm values in the app chart. here's the ES resource we applied (redacted):

```
apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1beta1
kind: ExternalSecret
metadata:
  name: staging-app-creds
  namespace: staging
spec:
  refreshInterval: "30s"
  secretStoreRef:
    name: vault-store
    kind: SecretStore
  target:
    name: staging-app-creds
    creationPolicy: Owner
  data:
  - secretKey: api_key
    remoteRef:
      key: secret/data/staging/app
      property: api_key
```

frank: that `creationPolicy: Owner` is the kicker if you also have TF managing the same Secret. Owner means ES tries to own and manage the k8s Secret; TF might try to reconcile its desired state and cause rapid churn or block updates.

maya: oh right — TF had a `kubernetes_manifest` for `Secret/staging-app-creds` from an older deploy. i'll remove it and try again. but curious why it took ~90s instead of immediate — operator logs show: `no change detected for remote secret (checksum match)`.

tom: checksum match log means either operator read the same data (so not changed) or there's a mismatch in how Vault KV v2 version is looked up. Did TF write to KV v2 via path `secret/data/...` (with data kv) vs operator expecting `secret/data/...`? versioning issues can produce stale reads if operator queries metadata version vs data.

nina: also check the operator's `syncInterval`/resync. Helm chart `values.syncInterval` default used to be 1m in some releases; `refreshInterval` on the CR is per-object but operator may still have leader resync debounce. ops-bot can dump chart values.

ops-bot: helm release "external-secrets" values: `controller.syncInterval: 1m`, `leaderElection.enabled: true`, operator image: v0.6.2.

frank: with controller sync 1m and CR refreshInterval 30s, effective behavior can still be one-minute-ish depending on leader loop and jitter. two fixes: bump `controller.syncInterval` to 15s (if you need faster) or set `refreshInterval` on the ES to 15s and ensure chart supports per-CR polling.

maya: removing the TF secret and reapplying now. I'll also set ES refreshInterval to "15s" for staging to confirm.

maya: update — removed TF secret, bumped refreshInterval to 15s, re-wrote the vault KV. secrets reconciled in ~10s. looks good.

nina: nice. for long-term: 1) avoid Terraform managing k8s Secrets that are target of ExternalSecrets (use TF to provision Vault data only). 2) document our chart's default syncInterval and override in envs that need faster propagation. 3) consider `creationPolicy: Merge` if you need TF to own specific keys.

tom: also watch for RBAC race — if ExternalSecrets controller doesn't have `vault:read` permission at the exact moment, it will log errors and retry on full sync interval. so check controller logs for `permission denied` if things still act flaky.

maya: will do. thanks all! :raised_hands:

frank: leaving a quick PR note: add a `docs/secrets.md` entry covering TF vs ExternalSecrets ownership and recommended `refreshInterval` defaults per env.

maya: thanks — that doc would help the on-call folks next time.
